plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce broad index concentration and cure the mandate breach.

This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged component.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL to 7%, SPAL to 6%, MUU to 6%, and METU to 6% to lean into leveraged ETFs.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for higher growth, potentially ~4%/month, by leaning into leverage and concentration. Be aware this significantly increases both upside and drawdown potential. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage rapid losses.

income.read: This income plan targets around ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
